title: Model Safety Packaging and Commercial Tiers Brief
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This brief defines a proposed product packaging and commercial model for offering graded model-safety guarantees as first-class, billable features in the Redwood product line. The goal is to make tradeoffs between cost, latency, and safety explicit to customers and to provide a clean upgrade path from low-friction, self-serve tiers to audit-ready enterprise offerings.

Background and motivation:
- Customers increasingly ask for configurable safety controls (content filtering, PII redaction, hallucination monitors, and provenance tagging) with predictable pricing and performance characteristics.
- Current safety capabilities are implemented as ad-hoc toggles across runtime, Optimize, and Console. Without packaging, customers either overpay or under-protect production workloads.
- Packaging safety as discrete tiers reduces integration friction for platform, clarifies SLA commitments, and enables new revenue streams that align with risk transfer (insurance-like economics).

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: classification of safety features, tier definitions, pricing multipliers, baseline SLOs associated with each tier, roadmap alignment, onboarding flow, telemetry and billing signals.
- Out of scope: low-level kernel/runtime changes to enforce per-token redaction (these are tracked in eng-serving-runtime design specs).

Overview of proposed safety tiers (customer-facing names):
1) Developer (Free / Low-cost)
   - Intended for experimentation and internal POCs.
   - Included safety features: basic profanity filter, lightweight rate-limits on safety scans.
   - Commitments: best-effort safety detection, no audit log retention.
   - Typical customers: early-stage startups and dev teams.

2) Production Shield (Standard)
   - For production applications with modest regulatory needs.
   - Included features: profanity & hate-speech filters, configurable PII redaction templates, built-in safety heuristics with tunable sensitivity.
   - Commitments: 30-day safety event retention, weekly quality report, incident-oriented rollback guidance.

3) Compliance Guard (Regulated)
   - For regulated verticals (healthcare, finance, legal) where auditability and retention are required.
   - Included features: deterministic PII redaction, signed provenance metadata, per-request sampling and capture, long-term audit logs (1 year), KMS-backed encryption for logs.
   - Commitments: SLA-backed safety processing success rate >= 99.9% for processed requests, response integrity proofs for captured outputs.

4) Enterprise Assurance (Custom)
   - Fully managed, white-glove offering with custom retention, HSM/KMS key custody options, SOC-level reporting, on-premises connectors, and compliance attestations.
   - Included features: bespoke mitigation pipelines, human-in-the-loop review workflows, contractually scoped safety error budgets.

Mapping of features to tier (table):
| Feature                          | Developer | Production Shield | Compliance Guard | Enterprise Assurance |
|----------------------------------|-----------|-------------------|------------------|----------------------|
| Profanity/basic filter           | ✓         | ✓                 | ✓                | ✓                    |
| PII redaction (heuristic)        | -         | ✓                 | ✓ (deterministic)| ✓                    |
| Signed provenance metadata       | -         | -                 | ✓                | ✓                    |
| Audit log retention (default)    | none      | 30d               | 365d             | custom               |
| KMS/HSM integration              | -         | -                 | optional         | required             |
| Human review workflow            | -         | opt-in            | opt-in           | managed              |

SLA and economics model:
- Baseline compute pricing remains per-token. Safety tiers are charged as a multiplier on token compute cost plus a fixed monthly safety feature fee for storage/retention and human review capacity where applicable.
- Initial suggested multipliers (configurable by region and model family):
  - Developer: x1.0 (no multiplier)
  - Production Shield: x1.08 (8% multiplier)
  - Compliance Guard: x1.25 (25% multiplier) + $0.02/GB-month audit log storage
  - Enterprise Assurance: bespoke pricing (baseline x1.35–x1.6, plus service fee)
- Justification: multipliers reflect additional per-request compute (safety pipeline scans + provenance signing), storage, and operational overhead. For Compliance Guard and Enterprise, we separate the storage line item on bills.

Operational design considerations:
- Runtime: safety pipelines should be implemented as execution stages that can be run synchronously or asynchronously depending on the tier. Synchronous enforcement (blocking output until redaction) is required for Compliance Guard and Enterprise Assurance; Production Shield may elect async filtering with compensating controls.
- Telemetry: safety_event.count, safety_event.latency_p50/p95, redaction.success_rate, provenance.attach_rate, human_review.queue_depth. All metrics must be emitted with the tenant tag and appended to per-tenant billing traces.
- Traceability: every request processed under a safety tier must carry a safety_policy_id and safety_execution_id. These are surfaced in the Console and included in audit exports.
- Storage: audit logs for Compliance Guard must be stored in encrypted, append-only buckets with retention policy enforcement and export APIs for compliance review.

Onboarding flow (customer-facing steps):
1) Self-serve sign-up: enable a safety tier toggle in Console during project creation.
2) Guided configuration: choose a policy template (PII-focused, content-moderation, HIPAA-lite).
3) Rollout: start in 'monitor-only' mode for 1–2 days, then opt-in to enforcement.
4) Audit validation: automated checks run against sample traffic, results displayed as pass/warn/fail.
5) Contract/upgrade: customers moving to Compliance Guard or Enterprise will require an order form and updated T&Cs.

Engineering rollout plan and milestones (high level):
- Q2 2025: Prototype policy templates, basic Console UX, and telemetry.
- Q3 2025: Implement synchronous enforcement path and retention-backed audit logs (Compliance Guard MVP).
- Q4 2025: Integrate KMS/HSM options, add provenance signing and export APIs.
- Q1 2026: Enterprise Assurance productization (billing plumbing, compliance kits, SOC-style artifacts).

Ownership and signoffs:
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner of the product brief and GTM alignment).
- Eng (runtime & platform): Marco Diaz (implementation plan and rollout windows).
- Security & Compliance: Ruth Chen (controls, evidence, and confidentiality requirements).
- Finance: Priya Kapoor (pricing validation and billing signals).

Release checklist (pre-publish to customers):
1) Required docs: public product brief, admin Console copy, and internal runbook.
2) Telemetry: baseline dashboards created (safety_event.* and retention costs).
3) Billing: test invoices for each tier and storage line items verified in sandbox.
4) Compliance: security assessment of audit log storage and key management.
5) Support: runbook for safety incidents and customer escalations published.

Migration guidance for existing customers:
- Default mapping: customers currently using ad-hoc safety toggles are mapped to Production Shield by default and notified with a migration window of 90 days.
- Migration tools: Console export/import for safety policies, a CLI tool to bulk-assign projects to tiers, and a simulation mode for verifying expected cost impact.

Monitoring & KPIs (product success metrics):
- Conversion rate from Developer -> Production Shield within 60 days of sign-up.
- Safety incident re-open rate for Compliance Guard customers (target < 0.5%).
- Average added latency introduced by safety pipelines (target <= 15% p95 increase for Production Shield).
- Incremental revenue contribution from safety tier multipliers and storage fees (monthly).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers perceive safety multipliers as opaque price increases. Mitigation: publish a clear cost calculator in Console and simulate before upgrade.
- Risk: Synchronous enforcement increases p95 latency for latency-sensitive apps. Mitigation: offer async enforcement for Production Shield with compensating visibility and retry semantics.
- Risk: Data residency and retention requirements differ by customer. Mitigation: provide region-scoped audit storage and retention rules configurable per-tenant.

Appendices:
A. Example Console policy JSON (policy template - PII redaction):
{
  "policy_id": "pii-redact-v1",
  "description": "Detect and redact common PII types (emails, SSNs, phone numbers)",
  "rules": [
    { "type": "regex", "pattern": "\\b[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}\\b", "action": "redact" },
    { "type": "ner", "labels": ["EMAIL", "PHONE_NUMBER"], "action": "redact" }
  ]
}

B. Example billing sample CLI to preview cost delta:
# Preview cost increase when upgrading a project to Compliance Guard
redwood billing preview --project my-app --upgrade-tier compliance-guard --window 30d

C. Related architecture pages:
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture: detailed safety stage contracts
- security-and-compliance/audit-logging: audit storage encryption standards

Next steps (action items):
- Product to finalize tier names and multipliers (owner: Aisha) by 2025-04-15.
- Eng to produce a feasibility estimate for synchronous enforcement per model family by 2025-04-30.
- Finance to validate billing plumbing for storage line items in sandbox by 2025-05-10.
